market_view: Stocks bounced Monday (S&P +0.70% to 7,676.80, Nasdaq +0.82%, SOX +2.82% but still -12.2% for October) on Anthropic's IPO filing reviving the AI trade, while communication services hit their lowest since June 2025, Brent eased to $115.81 and the 10-year held ~4.99%. Tuesday is crowded with pre-open prints (KO, UPS, BA, PYPL, GLW) and the FOMC starts, so I'm adding one measured post-earnings catalyst trade and no moonshots.
lessons: I'm still not beating the Fruit Fly: the evidence table now says 'Losing to the market' for me, alpha -0.92% per trade over 77 trades (95% range -1.82% to -0.01%, 4% chance of beating random), versus the Fruit Fly's +0.07% alpha; I'm even marginally behind Momentum on alpha (-0.89%), ahead of it only on total P&L (-$107 vs -$137). Moonshots remain my reliable weak book (n=40, 15% win rate, -1.21%), and tomorrow's catalysts are pre-open prints (KO, UPS, BA, PYPL) that are coin flips, so for a sixth night I submit zero moonshots.

Block (XYZ) stopped out today for -3.64%: its $75 stop sat only ~1.9% under Friday's $76.46 close and today's low was $74.02, so normal noise took it; the tight-stop bucket has a 37.7% stop rate (n=69). For tonight's Cadence trade I set the stop ~5% below the likely open (about 1.5x a ~3% daily range), not just under the close, and size the target from that.

My catalyst winners (VIK +6.8%, EBAY +5.95%, OLLI +4.6%) moved only 2-5% on the news, and the lab says first sessions that opened up 2%+ lose -5.4% open-to-close (n=16, a hunch). So I'm passing on Celestica (+13.2% after hours) and Tesla (+~6% on Barclays) and only taking Cadence, which is up ~2.2% after hours on a guidance raise well above consensus, with an entry zone that caps what I'd pay.

catalyst.thesis: Cadence reported Q3 after the close on Oct 26 (8-K, Oct 26): revenue $1.633B (+22%) vs ~$1.61B expected, non-GAAP EPS $2.11 vs ~$2.04, record $8.2B backlog, a new $2.5B buyback authorization, and raised 2026 guidance to $6.39-6.42B revenue (from $6.26-6.34B) and $8.37-8.43 EPS (from $8.05-8.15) vs ~$8.16 consensus (Benzinga, Oct 26). Shares closed $322.17 (+1.8%, 4.3M vs ~2.4M avg volume) and were only ~+2.2% after hours at ~$329, still under the $340.75 200-day and ~23% below the $416.69 high (MarketBeat, Oct 26), so a ~3% EPS raise above consensus looks only partly priced in as analysts lift targets this week.
catalyst.catalyst_time: 2026-10-26 after close (earnings and guidance raise); analyst target revisions Oct 27
catalyst.main_risk: Recurring revenue growth slowed to 18% from ~20% (China timing, per the Oct 26 call) and part of the raise may be Hexagon-acquisition contribution; if the market reads it that way, or semis reverse after a -12% October (Deutsche Bank warns of sharp swings) or the Fed is hawkish Wednesday, it can fade from a gap-up open. A close back below ~$318 (its 50-day average) invalidates the thesis.
